calls.head: Depth against star power
calls.body: On depth, Utah sits 1st of 32, at the deep end of the scale. New Jersey is 31st, at the top-heavy end.
calls.call: Utah spreads its forward ice time deeper down the lineup than New Jersey.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On bottom-six share of forward ice time, Utah had 47% and New Jersey 42%. Coming in, Utah was at 44% and New Jersey at 40%.

calls.head: Bruisers against finesse
calls.body: On physicality, Utah sits 5th of 32, at the bruising end of the scale. New Jersey is 30th, at the finesse end.
calls.call: Utah hits more than New Jersey in the close stretches of the game.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: On hit score in close games (arena-adjusted, 100 is league average), Utah had 111 and New Jersey 57. Coming in, Utah was at 112 and New Jersey at 82.

NJD.head: We had this close to even (55% for New Jersey), and it went Utah’s way.

UTA.head: We had this close to even (45% for Utah), and Utah came through.

surprises.head: Utah’s power play came alive
surprises.body: Utah’s power play created 14.7 expected goals per 60, against its usual 8.0 and a league average of 7.5. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 15 games.

surprises.head: New Jersey tried a different line
surprises.body: A. Lombardi, C. Glass, J. Boqvist played 7:43 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of New Jersey’s usual lines.
